history.note: The hub has 117 items, almost all empty 'Untitled' designs (0 features, origin 'saved', 193-byte .fox). Overnight they appeared at 02:53, 02:56, 02:57, 03:01 (x4), 03:06, 03:07, 03:08 and 03:09, each logged as 'created Untitled'. Not caused by idling (90 s, none), a click on the canvas, launching a second instance, or fissionoxide-cli info/render. Some UI path is calling hub.save (data_panel.rs:933) on an empty untitled design; it lines up with the window being activated or a file being forwarded. Fix the trigger, and don't hub.save an empty, unnamed design without the user asking.

Root cause found 2026-10-20 09:05: the junk comes from cargo test runs, not the UI. Tests that save via the UI path fall back to Store::default_root() (the real %APPDATA% hub) unless FOX_DATA_DIR is set; the hub grew 116 -> 241 while agents ran tests. PR #100 guards the UI side; parity/ui-test-hub-isolation isolates tests.

Root cause: fox-engine test tests::every_listed_command_is_handled runs every command (including hub.save) on a Session with no store_root, so each test run wrote empty 'Untitled' designs into the real %APPDATA% hub (38 hub touches per run). name: wheel zoom direction
fusion: With default preferences (Reverse zoom direction off), rolling the wheel toward you (down) zooms in and rolling it away (up) zooms out, toward the cursor.

history.note: FissionOxide zooms the other way: wheel down zooms out (viewport.rs navigate(): factor = exp(-scroll.y*0.0015*zoom_sign), with reverse_zoom false). Fusion with Reverse zoom unchecked (checked on this machine's Preferences) zooms in on wheel down. Flip the default sign so the unchecked default matches Fusion, and keep the checkbox meaning 'reverse from Fusion's default'. Users with reverse_zoom already saved need their setting to keep the direction they chose.

name: copy paste
fusion: Ctrl+C then Ctrl+V on a component pastes a new occurrence (Arm:2) and opens the Initial Position dialog (Move Type, Set Pivot, X/Y/Z Distance, X/Y/Z Angle) with the triad, to place it; Cancel removes the paste. Ctrl+Shift+V (Paste New) makes an independent copy. On bodies and on sketch curves inside a sketch, Ctrl+V pastes a copy and opens Move/Copy.

history.note: FissionOxide has no copy/paste. Selecting Body1 and pressing Ctrl+C, Ctrl+V does nothing; lib.rs only binds V (without Ctrl). Fusion places pasted components and bodies with a triad dialog. The engine already has component.copy (Duplicate Component) and the Move dialog to build on.

name: fillet flow
fusion: Sketch Fillet: no side dialog. Click a corner (or two curves) and the fillet previews at once, with a heads-up radius box at the arc (default 5 mm here) and a drag arrow. Enter or a click accepts it, and the tool stays active for the next corner. Tooltip: 'Select first line or arc'.

history.note: FissionOxide opens a docked SKETCH FILLET dialog (Lines: Select, Radius 2 mm, OK/Cancel). Clicking the corner set the status bar to '2 objects', but the Lines row still read 'Select' and nothing previewed: no arc, no heads-up radius box at the corner, no drag arrow. Match Fusion's in-canvas flow and its 5 mm default, and keep the tool active after each fillet.

name: review warning
fusion: A failed feature's timeline icon gets a red frame, and a red error badge appears at the canvas's lower right. Right-clicking the icon adds Review Warning (red icon) to the menu (Create Selection Set, Edit Feature, Configure, Delete, Rename, Roll Timeline Marker Here, Convert to DM Feature, Suppress Features, Review warning, Find in Browser, Find in Window). It opens an Error window with a tree, Fillet1 > Compute Failed > an explanatory message (for example 'The fillet/chamfer could not be created where edges meet at a corner... Try adjusting the size...'), a copy button and Close. Clicking the badge opens the same window for all failures.

history.note: FissionOxide marks failed features in the timeline (ui:timeline:error-badges match), but the timeline menu has no Review Warning item, there's no Error window with the per-feature message tree and copy button, and the canvas has no error badge that lists every failure. The engine's error strings should feed the window's messages, phrased like Fusion's. Scene: a box with all edges filleted by parameter filletR, then filletR raised from 2 mm to 8 mm.
